registry_note: Resolve the registry through npa.deploy.images / npa configure. Additive tags are pushed to both the primary (eu-north1) and mirror (us-central1) registries; never hardcode a registry id here.

target.rt_cores_note: Datacenter Blackwell has no RT cores, exactly like H100/H200. Rasterized rendering (Isaac Lab / SONIC isaac-render) must stay on L40S or RTX PRO 6000; only headless / state-based work routes here.
target.sass_compatibility: SASS is per-arch with no cross-major compatibility. sm_120 (major 12, RTX PRO 6000) binaries and sm_100/sm_103 (major 10) binaries are mutually incompatible, so validating on RTX PRO 6000 does not prove B200/B300. Within a major, minor-version forward compatibility holds: sm_100 SASS runs on sm_103, not the reverse. Build for sm_100 first and confirm on B300.
arch_knobs: Prebuilt torch wheels ship a fixed fat-binary arch set that TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST cannot change; only the wheel index does. cu128/cu130 include sm_100 and sm_120, cu124/cu126 stop at sm_90.

Source-compiled CUDA extensions (flash-attn from source, Taichi/Genesis, natten, custom ops) obey TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST. Omitting an arch yields 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device' at runtime.

verdicts.ready: The base wheel/toolchain already covers sm_100, so the image needs an additive rebuild plus live validation - no dependency changes.
verdicts.port: Needs a CUDA/torch bump or arch flags before it can target sm_100; the upstream wheels exist.
verdicts.blocked: Upstream does not ship the architecture yet. Track the upstream reason; never stub a fake pass.
verdicts.not-applicable: CPU-only or GPU-agnostic. It already runs on a B200/B300 host; only node-pool scheduling needs confirming.

validation_states.validated: get_device_capability() confirmed on a real B200/B300 node with the image's real capability smoke passing.
validation_states.pending-hardware: Wheel arch set confirmed, but not yet run on a real datacenter Blackwell node.
validation_states.not-required: CPU-only image; no arch assertion applies.

images.name: npa-base
images.smoke: import flash_attn; flash_attn_func on a real device
images.notes: Gates most of the tree, so it is built and validated first. TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST was widened from 10.3 to cover both CUDA majors; the build asserts the wheel reports sm_80/sm_90/sm_100/sm_120. sm_103 is intentionally not asserted because stock cu130 wheels ship sm_100 SASS and B300 is reached by 10.0 -> 10.3 forward compat. flash-attn-4 CuTe JIT-compiles at runtime, which is why it also runs on sm_120 - that JIT assumption still needs confirming on real B200/B300 silicon.

images.name: npa-lerobot
images.torch: 2.12.1 (bundled cu128) on the default Dockerfile; inherited 2.9.0+cu130 on Dockerfile.b300
images.smoke: ACT training step on lerobot/pusht
images.notes: Highest-confidence Blackwell path: Dockerfile.b300 is already labelled b300-sm_103 and B300 is Tier-1 in docs/nvidia-platform-architecture-coverage.md. The default Dockerfile starts from cu124 but pip-upgrades torch 2.12.1, so the effective arch set comes from the bundled cu128 wheel and is Blackwell-capable; prefer Dockerfile.b300 when reproducibility matters. Add B200 validation on top of the existing B300 evidence. Diffusion Policy is ~2.5x slower than H200 on B300 because it JITs from sm_100 PTX.

images.name: npa-genesis
images.blocked_reason: Genesis physics runs on Taichi, which has no stable sm_103 support. The torch side is portable (move the default off cu124 onto the cu130 Dockerfile.sm120 path), but the Taichi kernels are the hard gate.
images.upstream_tracking: Taichi CUDA codegen for Blackwell: https://github.com/taichi-dev/taichi/pull/8735 and https://github.com/taichi-dev/taichi/issues/8730. Retest sm_100 (B200) first - it may land before sm_103, and once Taichi accepts sm_103 the B300 case follows by forward compat.
images.smoke: gs.init(gpu) plus a FrankaPickPlaceEnv step
images.notes: Do not stub this. Re-test Taichi on B200 (sm_100) on each upstream release; that is the earliest signal. The whole sim2real subtree inherits this blocker.

images.name: npa-isaac-lab
images.blocked_reason: The NVIDIA vendor stack is pinned to x86_64 CUDA 12.8 with torch 2.7.0; B200/B300 support is gated on NVIDIA's x86_64 CUDA 13 alignment. Independently, Isaac Lab's value here is rasterized rendering, which datacenter Blackwell cannot do at all (no RT cores).
images.upstream_tracking: NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim release notes for x86_64 CUDA 13 alignment
images.smoke: headless RL training step (never a render task)
images.notes: Omniverse-restricted: never publish prebuilt to a public registry. Keep render workloads on L40S / RTX PRO 6000 regardless of what CUDA the vendor ships.

images.upstream_tracking: NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim release notes for x86_64 CUDA 13 alignment
images.smoke: headless whole-body-control fine-tune step
